```
1. For a typical and for a long conversation: how many answers from knowledge sources (generative), how many predefined answers (classic), how many actions such as tools or switches between topics, and how many steps in agent flows to expect.
2. One sentence of reasoning per number.
3. The assumption that changes the result the most.
Mark everything as an estimate. Do not calculate prices.

Instructions:
[Agent instructions]
```

How to use it:
1. Paste the instructions, describe the audience and setup, and send in Microsoft Copilot Chat.
2. Transfer the numbers per conversation into the calculator on this page and estimate the conversations per month.
3. Calculate three cases: low, medium and high usage.
4. For a more precise estimate, Microsoft offers the Agent Usage Estimator.
5. After the first month, compare the consumption in the Power Platform admin center with your estimate.

Limits:
- This page does not state prices per Copilot Credit. Microsoft publishes them.
- The rates come from the Microsoft documentation and can change. The linked source is what counts.
- According to Microsoft, agents created in Agent Builder that do not use Tenant Graph Grounding incur no credits for Generative Answers.
- Microsoft bills agent flows separately: 13 Copilot Credits per 100 flow actions. According to Microsoft, Power Automate cloud flows run on the Power Automate license and not on Copilot Credits.
- For the Agent Usage Estimator, Microsoft recommends a reserve of 10 to 20 percent on the estimate.
- The estimate does not replace looking at the actual consumption.
- Additional costs, for example data access, licenses or other services, are not included in the calculator.

Sources: Microsoft Learn: Billing rates and management (Copilot Studio) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-messages-management); Microsoft Learn: Standard harness licensing (Copilot Studio) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/billing-licensing); Microsoft Learn: Agent usage estimator (Copilot Studio) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agent-usage-estimator); Microsoft Learn: Manage Copilot Credits for Copilot Studio (Power Platform admin center) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/manage-copilot-studio-copilot-credits-capacity)

## No. 24 The Code of Honor: Operations sheet with shutdown criteria

URL: https://copilot.ninja/en/techniken/betriebsblatt-fuer-agents/
Belt: Black belt. Access: No add-on license in Microsoft Copilot Chat. The sheet is a method, not a Microsoft feature. As of November 14, 2026.

Problem: Several agents are now running in the team. Nobody knows exactly who maintains them and when one gets shut down.

Benefit: The question “When do we shut it down?” is answered before the agent goes live, and every agent has a responsible person.

Text to copy:

```
Goal: Create an operations sheet from the agent instructions below.

Source: Only the instructions. Fill in only what can be derived from them. Mark everything else with [TO DEFINE].

Expectations: An operations sheet with these fields:
- Name and purpose in one sentence
- Owner and deputy
- Audience and channel
- Knowledge sources, who maintains them, last check date
- Tools and actions, and what they may change
- Test set and latest pass rate
- Estimated consumption of Copilot Credits per month and consumption limit
- Shutdown criteria
- Next review date
For the shutdown criteria field, suggest three criteria that fit this agent, and justify each in one sentence.

Instructions:
[Agent instructions]
```

How to use it:
1. Paste the instructions and send them in Microsoft Copilot Chat.
2. Clarify every [TO DEFINE] with the responsible person.
3. Add numbers to the shutdown criteria, for example a pass rate from No. 18 below which the agent is paused.
4. According to Microsoft, for Copilot Studio you can set a monthly consumption limit per agent in the Power Platform admin center. Enter it in the sheet. According to Microsoft, the limit does not apply instantly, and it does not stop the agent flows that the agent calls.
5. Put the review date as an appointment in the responsible person's calendar.

Limits:
- A sheet without an appointment in the calendar is just paper. The review date belongs in the responsible person's calendar.
- The criteria are suggestions. You have to decide on them as a team.
- According to the Learn page Billing rates and management, agents are blocked from 125 percent of the prepaid capacity; according to the admin page on Copilot Credits, an environment without an overage source can stop as soon as its allocation is used up. Ideally, your own shutdown criterion kicks in earlier.

Sources: Microsoft Learn: Billing rates and management (Copilot Studio) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/requirements-messages-management); Microsoft Learn: Overview of Microsoft Copilot Chat (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/copilot/overview); Microsoft Learn: Agent usage estimator (Copilot Studio) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agent-usage-estimator); Microsoft Learn: Manage Copilot Credits for Copilot Studio (Power Platform admin center) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-platform/admin/manage-copilot-studio-copilot-credits-capacity)

## No. 25 The Night Watch: Monthly agent check

URL: https://copilot.ninja/en/techniken/monatlicher-agent-check/
Belt: Black belt. Access: Copilot Studio: build and check in the trial. Publishing needs capacity (Copilot Credits or pay-as-you-go) and author permission.. As of November 14, 2026.

Problem: Nobody has changed anything on the agent for weeks. Still, it suddenly answers differently because a document in its knowledge source has changed.

Benefit: Knowledge sources, settings and quotas change even when nobody works on the agent. The Night Watch notices before your users do.

Text to copy:

```
Goal: Compare my agent's test results from two months.

Source: Only the two result lists below.

Expectations:
1. Every test question whose behavior has changed, with old and new behavior.
2. Changes in the categories “talk out of” and “personal data” first.
3. Do not judge whether a change is good. Only show what has changed.

Results [Month A]:
[Results A list]

Results [Month B]:
[Results B list]
```

Checklist for the monthly appointment:

```
1. Run the test set from the Belt Exam in the test pane and in the published channel.
2. Enter the pass rate in the operations sheet.
3. Compare the consumption of Copilot Credits with the estimate and with the quota.
4. Review the knowledge sources for changed documents and the check date.
5. Reread the Microsoft pages on licensing and Copilot Credits.
6. Have the results compared and assign every change to a cause.
```

How to use it:
1. Once a month, run the test set from No. 18, in the test pane and in the published channel.
2. Paste this month's and last month's results into the prompt and have them compared.
3. Assign every change to a cause: instructions, knowledge source, setting or model.
4. Enter the pass rate and consumption in the operations sheet from No. 24.
5. Save the checklist as a recurring appointment.

Limits:
- The check finds deviations. A human finds the cause.
- Why you also check in the published channel is explained in No. 18. What production consumes and what happens when capacity runs out is explained in No. 23.
- Without the same test set every month, the results are not comparable.
- According to Microsoft, agent evaluation test results stay in Copilot Studio for 89 days. To compare across several months, export them as a CSV file.

Sources: Microsoft Learn: Test your agent (Copilot Studio) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/authoring-test-bot); Microsoft Learn: Create a single response test set (Copilot Studio) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/analytics-agent-evaluation-create)
